questions.question: Match the following parties with their reserved symbols and choose the INCORRECT one among the following:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**All India Trinamool Congress – Sickle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reserved symbol of the **All India Trinamool Congress (AITC)** is not a sickle but **Flowers and Grass**.
 
• The **symbol** of Flowers and Grass represents the party's commitment to its grassroots approach and policies.
 
• Founded by **Mamata Banerjee** in 1998, the AITC is primarily active in the state of **West Bengal**.
 
• The party has been recognized as a **national party** by the Election Commission of India due to its significant presence in multiple states.
 
• The incorrect association of the sickle symbol could lead to confusion as the sickle is more commonly associated with **leftist or communist ideologies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National People’s Party – Book**__

 __
 
• The **National People’s Party (NPP)** uses the symbol of a **Book**, which signifies education, knowledge, and enlightenment.
 
• The NPP is primarily based in the northeastern state of **Meghalaya**.
 
• Founded by **P.A. Sangma** in 2013, the NPP is the first political party from the Northeast to achieve the status of a **national party**.
 
 
 
• **Bahujan Samaj Party – Elephant**__
 __
 
• The symbol of the **Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)** is an **Elephant**, representing strength and the oppressed sections of society.
 
• The BSP was founded by **Kanshi Ram** in 1984 and is primarily focused on the welfare of **Scheduled Castes (Dalits), Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes (OBCs).**
 
• The party is headquartered in **New Delhi** and has a strong political presence in the state of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Nationalist Congress Party – Clock**__
 
 
• The **Nationalist Congress Party (NCP)** has the reserved symbol of a **Clock**, symbolizing time and progress.
 
• Founded in 1999 by **Sharad Pawar**, the NCP is headquartered in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
• The party focuses on promoting **secularism, democracy, and federalism.**

questions.question: What do you call the body cavity that is lined by mesoderm?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Coelom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **coelom** is a body cavity that is completely lined by the **mesoderm**, the middle layer of embryonic tissue in triploblastic animals.
 
• This cavity is filled with fluid and provides a space for the development and suspension of internal organs, allowing them to grow and move independently of the body wall.
 
• Coelomates, or animals with a coelom, exhibit a higher level of structural complexity and specialization in organ systems compared to animals without a coelom.
 
• The presence of a coelom is a key characteristic of many higher animal groups, including **annelids, mollusks, arthropods, echinoderms, and chordates**.
 
• The coelom plays an essential role in functions such as **circulation, respiration, and waste elimination** by providing space for the development of complex systems like the digestive and cardiovascular systems.
 
• The coelom also acts as a cushion for internal organs, protecting them from mechanical shocks and injuries.
 
• It allows the body to have a more flexible and efficient movement due to its role in forming a hydrostatic skeleton in some organisms like earthworms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diploblasts**__

 __
 
• **Diploblastic animals** are organisms that develop from two embryonic germ layers: the **ectoderm and endoderm**.
 
• They lack a mesoderm, which means they do not develop a true coelom. Examples include **cnidarians** like jellyfish and corals.
 
• These organisms usually have a simple body structure and radial symmetry.
 
 
 
• **Radial Symmetry**__
 __
 
• **Radial symmetry** refers to a body plan in which any plane passing through the central axis divides the organism into identical halves.
 
• This type of symmetry is seen in animals like **cnidarians** (e.g., jellyfish) and **echinoderms** (e.g., starfish in their larval stage).
 
• It is associated with animals that have a sessile or free-floating lifestyle.
 
 
 
• **Triploblasts**__
 
 
• **Triploblastic animals** are organisms that develop from three embryonic germ layers: the **ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm**.
 
• They can be further categorized as **acoelomates (without a coelom), pseudocoelomates, or coelomates** based on the presence and type of coelom.
 
• Examples include most higher animals like **arthropods, mollusks, and vertebrates**.

questions.question: With reference to provinces under Mauryan dynasty, which of the following pairs is correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Prachyapatha (East) - Toshali**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **provinces under the Mauryan dynasty** were administratively divided to ensure effective governance. Each province was headed by a governor.
 
• **Toshali**, located in the **eastern region**, was a prominent province under the Mauryan Empire. It falls under the category of **Prachyapatha (East).**
 
• The Mauryan administration prioritized the division of territories based on their **geographical significance** and ensured proper governance through regional centers.
 
• **Edicts of Ashoka** discovered in Toshali indicate its importance as a provincial capital during the Mauryan era.
 
• Toshali played a crucial role in managing the **eastern territories** and facilitating trade and communication with neighboring regions.
 
• The Mauryan Empire was known for its **efficient administrative system**, with provinces being an integral part of its governance model.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dakshinapatha (South) - Ujjain**__

 __
 
• **Ujjain** was located in the western part of India and served as a key center for trade and administration.
 
• It was an important city under the Mauryan dynasty but was not part of the **southern province, Dakshinapatha.**
 
• Ujjain is traditionally associated with the **Avantiratha (West).**
 
 
 
• **Uttarapatha (North) - Suvarnagiri**__
 __
 
• **Suvarnagiri** was known for its **gold mines** and was located in the southern region, not the northern province of Uttarapatha.
 
• The northern province, Uttarapatha, was associated with regions like **Taxila.**
 
 
 
• **Avantiratha (West) - Taxila**__
 
 
• **Taxila**, a renowned center of learning and culture, was part of the northern province of **Uttarapatha**, not the western province Avantiratha.
 
• Taxila was a significant city under Mauryan rule and played a key role in trade and education.

questions.question:
Meher had two large chunks of coal. She set fire to the first chunk and broke the second one into pieces. Help Meher understand what kind of changes happened to the two chunks of coal at the end of the activity by choosing all the applicable statements.

A. Both chunks of coal underwent physical changes only.

B. The changes were reversible for the first chunk of coal only.

C. Only physical changes took place for the second chunk of coal.

D. Both chunks of coal underwent chemical changes only.

E. The first case is an example of chemical changes.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only C and E**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first chunk of coal was set on fire, which led to a **chemical change**. Burning coal results in the production of heat, light, and gases like carbon dioxide. This is a chemical change because the coal is transformed into new substances, and the change is irreversible.
 
• The second chunk of coal was broken into smaller pieces. Breaking coal into pieces is a **physical change** because it only alters the size or shape of the coal without affecting its chemical composition. This type of change is reversible.
 
• Option **C** correctly identifies that only a **physical change** took place for the second chunk of coal.
 
• Option **E** is accurate in stating that the first case demonstrates a **chemical change**, as burning involves a transformation of substances.
 
• The distinction between physical and chemical changes is important in understanding the properties and behavior of materials under different conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option A: Both chunks of coal underwent physical changes only**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect because the first chunk of coal underwent a **chemical change** due to combustion, while only the second chunk experienced a **physical change**.
 
 
 
• **Option B: The changes were reversible for the first chunk of coal only**__
 __
 
• This is inaccurate because the change in the first chunk (burning coal) is irreversible, as it transforms into new substances.
 
 
 
• **Option D: Both chunks of coal underwent chemical changes only**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because the second chunk of coal only experienced a **physical change** (breaking into smaller pieces), not a chemical change.

questions.question: As per the 2011 census, which of the following union territories had the lowest population?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lakshadweep** is the smallest Union Territory of India in terms of **population**, as per the **2011 Census**.
 
• The total population of Lakshadweep, according to the 2011 Census, was **64,429**.
 
• It is a group of **36 islands** located in the **Arabian Sea**, off the southwestern coast of India.
 
• The islands are known for their **pristine beauty**, **coral reefs**, and **marine biodiversity**.
 
• Kavaratti is the **capital** of Lakshadweep and also one of the most developed islands in the region.
 
• The Union Territory has a predominantly **Muslim population**, with **Malayalam** and **Jeseri** (a dialect of Malayalam) being the widely spoken languages.
 
• Tourism is a significant activity in Lakshadweep due to its **natural beauty**, but it is regulated to preserve the fragile ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__

 __
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are located in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• These islands are larger in terms of area and population compared to Lakshadweep.
 
• As per the **2011 Census**, the population was approximately **380,581**.
 
• Port Blair is the **capital** of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• These islands are known for their **tribal communities, dense forests, and historical significance**, such as the infamous **Cellular Jail**.
 
 
 
• **Chandigarh**__
 __
 
• **Chandigarh** is a Union Territory and the **capital city** of both Punjab and Haryana.
 
• It is known for its **modern architecture** and was designed by **Le Corbusier**, a Swiss-French architect.
 
• As per the **2011 Census**, Chandigarh had a population of approximately **1,055,450**.
 
• The city is also a hub for **education, industry, and administration**.
 
 
 
• **Puducherry**__
 
 
• **Puducherry**, formerly known as **Pondicherry**, is a Union Territory in southern India.
 
• It is known for its **French colonial heritage**, evident in its architecture and culture.
 
• As per the **2011 Census**, Puducherry had a population of approximately **1,247,953**.
 
• The Union Territory comprises four regions: **Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam**.
 
• The region is popular for its **beaches, temples, and Auroville**, an experimental township for sustainable living.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: With which of the following organisations was Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher of Hindu College of Calcutta, associated?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Young Bengal Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio**, a teacher at **Hindu College, Calcutta**, is considered the founder of the **Young Bengal Movement**.
 
• The movement was started in the **early 19th century** in Bengal and was inspired by the ideals of the **French Revolution** and the principles of **rationality, liberty, and freedom of thought.**
 
• Derozio and his followers, known as the **Derozians**, emphasized **secularism, scientific thinking, and social reform.**
 
• The movement criticized the **orthodox and superstitious practices** prevalent in Indian society at that time.
 
• The members of the Young Bengal Movement were noted for their efforts to promote **education, women's rights, and freedom of expression.**
 
• Derozio encouraged his students to question established norms and adopt a more **progressive and liberal outlook.**
 
• The movement played a pivotal role in shaping the **social and intellectual awakening** that later became part of the **Bengal Renaissance.**
 
• Though the movement faced criticism for being too radical and failed to achieve widespread popularity, its legacy lies in its contribution to the **modernization of Indian society.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Paramahansa Mandali**__

 __
 
• The **Paramahansa Mandali** was a secret socio-religious group founded in **1849 in Bombay (Mumbai).**
 
• It worked to promote **monotheism** and challenged **caste discrimination and idol worship.**
 
• The members were inspired by **Vedantic philosophy** and aimed to bring about social reform, particularly in areas such as **women’s rights and untouchability.**
 
 
 
• **Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam**__
 __
 
• Founded in **1903 in Kerala**, this organization was established by **Sree Narayana Guru**.
 
• It aimed to promote **social equality, education, and the upliftment of marginalized communities.**
 
• The organization is known for its slogan: **"One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man."**
 
 
 
• **Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha**__
 
 
• It was a **reformist Zoroastrian organization** founded in **1851 in Bombay (Mumbai)** by prominent Parsi leaders.
 
• The Sabha aimed to bring reforms to **Parsi religious practices** and worked for the **educational and social advancement** of the Parsi community.

questions.question: In which of the following empires of South India was the Kamalapuram tank built in the 15th century?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vijayanagara Empire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kamalapuram tank** is a well-known water reservoir constructed during the reign of the **Vijayanagara Empire** in the 15th century.
 
• This tank was built to provide **irrigation facilities** and to meet the **water needs of the capital city**, Hampi, which was one of the richest and most powerful cities of its time.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was renowned for its **advanced water management systems**, including tanks, canals, and aqueducts, which were vital for agriculture and urban needs.
 
• The Kamalapuram tank is located near the **Virupaksha Temple** and other significant architectural marvels of Hampi, showcasing the empire's focus on both functionality and aesthetics.
 
• It is an example of the **sophisticated engineering** and planning that characterized the Vijayanagara Empire, reflecting their understanding of **hydrology and sustainable practices**.
 
• The tank played an important role in maintaining the city's **agricultural productivity** and providing water to its residents, making it a critical component of the empire's infrastructure.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646 CE) was one of the most significant empires in South India, known for its **architectural achievements**, **cultural contributions**, and **military prowess**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bidar Empire**__

 __
 
• The Bidar Sultanate was part of the **Deccan Sultanates** and was established in the 15th century.
 
• Bidar is known for its **fort** and **Bidriware** (a form of metal handicraft).
 
• Though the Bidar Sultanate contributed to architecture and culture, it did not play a significant role in water management like the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Bijapur Empire**__
 __
 
• The Bijapur Sultanate, another member of the **Deccan Sultanates**, is renowned for its **Islamic architecture**, including the iconic **Gol Gumbaz**.
 
• While Bijapur excelled in architecture, its contributions were more focused on **monuments** rather than large-scale water management systems like those in the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Chola Empire**__
 
 
• The Chola Empire (9th–13th century CE) is famous for its **temple architecture**, such as the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Tamil Nadu.
 
• They were pioneers in **irrigation systems**, particularly in the Kaveri delta, but the Kamalapuram tank was not part of their contributions as it was built much later during the Vijayanagara period.

questions.question: In May 2023, who was sworn in as the new Central Vigilance Commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**PK Srivastava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PK Srivastava** was sworn in as the **new Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC)** of India in May 2023.
 
• The **Central Vigilance Commission** is an apex Indian governmental body created in 1964 to address governmental corruption.
 
• The CVC operates as an independent authority and is responsible for monitoring and advising on all vigilance activities under the central government of India.
 
• **PK Srivastava** succeeded **Suresh N Patel**, who served as the previous Central Vigilance Commissioner.
 
• He brings extensive experience in the field of **administration and vigilance**, which is critical for curbing corruption and ensuring transparency in governance.
 
• The appointment of the CVC is made by the President of India based on the recommendation of a committee comprising the **Prime Minister, the Home Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition**.
 
• The tenure of the Central Vigilance Commissioner is **four years** or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CVC plays a pivotal role in ensuring the implementation of the **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988** and other relevant anti-corruption laws in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **GC Murmu**__

 __
 
• **GC Murmu** has served as the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India**. He was appointed as the 14th CAG of India in August 2020.
 
• The CAG is responsible for auditing the accounts of the central and state governments and ensuring accountability in the use of public funds.
 
 
 
• **Amit Khare**__
 __
 
• **Amit Khare** is a retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer known for his role in exposing the **fodder scam** in Bihar during his tenure as a district magistrate.
 
• He served as the **Information and Broadcasting Secretary** and later as the **Education Secretary** of India.
 
 
 
• **Suresh N Patel**__
 
 
• **Suresh N Patel** was the **previous Central Vigilance Commissioner** of India, serving until May 2023.
 
• He was known for his efforts to strengthen vigilance mechanisms and promote ethical governance during his tenure.

questions.question: Gangubai Hangal, a renowned Indian music personality, is recognised for her contributions in which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hindustani Classical Music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gangubai Hangal** was a legendary figure in the field of **Hindustani Classical Music**.
 
• She was born in **Karnataka** in 1913 and is widely regarded as one of the greatest exponents of the **Kirana Gharana**.
 
• She primarily specialized in the **Khyal** style of Hindustani classical singing, which emphasizes improvisation and exploration of ragas.
 
• Her voice was known for its **depth** and **richness**, which were used to bring out the intricate nuances of ragas.
 
• Throughout her career, she received numerous accolades, including the **Padma Bhushan** (1971) and the **Padma Vibhushan** (2002), which are among India's highest civilian honors.
 
• Gangubai Hangal performed at various prestigious music festivals and was instrumental in popularizing Hindustani classical music among newer generations.
 
• She also served as an inspiration for women in music, having overcome significant challenges, including social and cultural barriers, during her journey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rabindra Sangeet**__

 __
 
• **Rabindra Sangeet** refers to the songs written and composed by **Rabindranath Tagore**, a renowned poet, writer, and composer from **Bengal**.
 
• It combines elements of **Indian classical music** with folk traditions and often carries deep philosophical or emotional themes.
 
• Rabindra Sangeet is a distinct genre and is highly popular in **Bengal** and other parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Sufi Music**__
 __
 
• **Sufi Music** is a form of devotional music that originates from the traditions of **Sufism**, a mystical branch of Islam.
 
• It often seeks to express spiritual longing and divine love through poetry and melodies.
 
• Popular Sufi singers include **Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan** and **Abida Parveen**.
 
 
 
• **Ghazal Singing**__
 
 
• **Ghazal** is a poetic form that originated in **Persian literature** and later flourished in South Asia.
 
• **Ghazal Singing** involves the musical rendition of these poems, often focusing on themes of love, loss, and spirituality.
 
• Famous Ghazal singers include **Jagjit Singh** and **Mehdi Hassan**.

questions.question: On 19 July 2023, who was appointed as the 25th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rakesh Pal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rakesh Pal** was appointed as the **25th Director General** of the **Indian Coast Guard (ICG)** on **19 July 2023**.
 
• He is the first officer from the **Indian Coast Guard** to be elevated to the position of Director General, marking a significant milestone for the organization.
 
• He has served in various capacities within the **Indian Coast Guard**, such as the **Additional Director General** and **Commander of the Western Seaboard**.
 
• His extensive experience includes overseeing **operations, administration, and maritime safety**, making him highly suitable for the role of Director General.
 
• The **Indian Coast Guard** is responsible for safeguarding India’s **maritime interests** and enforcing maritime law within the country’s territorial waters.
 
• Under his leadership, the Indian Coast Guard is expected to enhance its capabilities in areas such as **maritime security, search and rescue operations, and environmental protection**.
 
• The **Indian Coast Guard** was established in **1977** and operates under the **Ministry of Defence**, playing a crucial role in national security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **BS Raju**__

 __
 
• **BS Raju** is a senior officer in the **Indian Army**, but he is not associated with the Indian Coast Guard.
 
• He has held significant positions such as the **Vice Chief of the Indian Army**, contributing to the operational and administrative efficiency of the Army.
 
 
 
• **K Natarajan**__
 __
 
• **K Natarajan** was the **24th Director General** of the Indian Coast Guard, serving prior to Rakesh Pal.
 
• He played a pivotal role in strengthening the **operational capabilities** of the Coast Guard during his tenure.
 
 
 
• **VK Singh**__
 
 
• **VK Singh** is a retired **General of the Indian Army** and has also served as a **Minister of State in the Government of India**.
 
• He is not associated with the Indian Coast Guard but has contributed significantly to India’s **defense and governance sectors**.

questions.question: Which of the following National Waterways (NW) is associated with the Udyogamandal and the Champakkara canals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Waterway 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3)** is also known as the **West Coast Canal.**
 
• It is located in the state of **Kerala** and runs parallel to the western coastline of India.
 
• It connects the **Kottapuram-Kollam stretch**, along with the **Champakkara Canal** and the **Udyogamandal Canal.**
 
• The Champakkara Canal is used for the transportation of **goods and cargo** to the Kochi Port.
 
• The Udyogamandal Canal serves the **industrial belt** in Kerala, supporting industries with efficient waterway transport.
 
• NW-3 spans a total length of **168 km** and is a crucial inland waterway for Kerala's economic activities.
 
• This waterway facilitates **trade, transportation, and tourism** in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 10 (NW-10)**__

 __
 
• **National Waterway 10 (NW-10) **is located in **Maharashtra**, specifically on the Amba River.
 
• This waterway is important for the **transportation of goods and passengers** in the Sunderbans region.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 5 (NW-5)**__
 __
 
• **NW-5** is primarily located in the states of **Odisha and West Bengal**.
 
• It connects the **Brahmani River, Mahanadi River Delta, and East Coast Canal.**
 
• This waterway is significant for **coal transportation** from Odisha's mines to various industries.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 25 (NW-25)**__
 
 
• **NW-25** is a lesser-known waterway located in the **state of Karnataka.**
 
• It covers the **Sharavati River**, facilitating local transportation and economic activities.

questions.question: Most of the Harappan sites are primarily divided into ________ parts.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Most of the **Harappan sites** are primarily divided into **two parts:** the **Citadel** and the **Lower Town.**
 
• The **Citadel** was a raised area, often fortified, where rulers or elites lived. It contained large structures such as granaries, assembly halls, and possibly religious buildings.
 
• The **Lower Town** was the larger area meant for common people. It included houses, workshops, streets, and other facilities.
 
• The division into two parts reflects the **planned urban layout** of Harappan cities, showcasing their advanced knowledge of **town planning, drainage systems, and architecture.**
 
• Examples of this division can be observed at sites like **Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, and Dholavira.**
 
• The existence of a citadel highlights the presence of a **social hierarchy and administrative control** in Harappan civilization.
 
• The streets in Harappan cities were laid out in a **grid pattern**, with advanced drainage systems, indicating a high level of **civil engineering expertise.**
 
• The division also demonstrates the **importance of security** and the need to protect the elite and critical infrastructure from external threats or floods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indus Valley Civilization

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, flourishing around 2500 BCE.
 
• It was characterized by well-planned cities, advanced drainage systems, and impressive architectural structures.
 
• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• Harappan Trade
 
 
• Harappans engaged in extensive trade networks both within the Indian subcontinent and with distant lands like Mesopotamia, Persia, and the Arabian Peninsula.
 
• Goods traded included beads, pottery, cotton textiles, and precious stones.
 
 
 
• Harappan Architecture
 
 
• Harappan cities were known for their uniform grid patterns, with streets laid out in perfect right angles.
 
• Buildings were constructed using standardized baked bricks, and many structures featured intricate drainage systems.
 
 
 
• Archaeological Discoveries
 
 
• Excavations at Harappan sites have revealed a wealth of artifacts, including seals with inscriptions, weights and measures, and terracotta figurines.
 
• These discoveries provide valuable insights into the social, economic, and cultural aspects of the Harappan Civilization.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered as a Fundamental Duty?

options.text: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To uphold and protect secularism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Fundamental Duties** was introduced through the **42nd Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution in **1976**.
 
• Fundamental Duties are enumerated under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties primarily focus on the promotion of a sense of **patriotism** and strengthening the spirit of **unity and integrity** within the nation.
 
• While the duty to uphold and protect the **sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India** is explicitly mentioned in the Fundamental Duties, protecting secularism is not directly specified as a Fundamental Duty.
 
• Secularism is a part of the **Preamble** and is considered a core principle of the Indian Constitution but does not appear in the list of Fundamental Duties under **Article 51A**.
 
• India is a **secular state**, meaning that the government treats all religions equally, but ensuring secularism is a responsibility of the state rather than being categorized as a Fundamental Duty for citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture**__

 __
 
• This duty emphasizes the importance of protecting and preserving India’s **historical monuments, traditions, and diverse cultural heritage.**
 
• It is meant to foster respect for the **rich diversity** of India's composite culture.
 
 
 
• **To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India**__
 __
 
• This duty involves ensuring the **nation's security** and standing against any threats that aim to divide the country.
 
• It is considered crucial for maintaining **national stability** and harmony.
 
 
 
• **To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform**__
 
 
• This duty encourages citizens to adopt a rational and **scientific mindset**.
 
• It promotes the spirit of **innovation**, reform, and critical thinking to improve societal standards.
 
• The goal is to eliminate superstition and foster **progressive values**.

• These techniques were widely used before the advent of the **Fosbury Flop**, which revolutionized the high jump in the 1960s.
 
• The high jump is measured based on the height cleared by the jumper without displacing the bar.
 
• It is a key event in international competitions such as the **Olympics, World Athletics Championships,** and other regional athletic meets.
 
• Modern high jumpers use advanced techniques and training to optimize their performance, combining speed, flexibility, and strength.

• The event has different rules and measurement methods compared to the high jump.

 __

• Unlike the high jump, the pole vault incorporates the use of external tools (the pole) to achieve height.
